### Authority
Author: Chuck Swindoll
Site: Insight for Living
URL: https://insight.org/resources/daily-devotional/authority?ga=testimonial-resources
Passage: Genesis 4:7
Points:
- Cain displayed stubborn rebellion against God when his sacrifice was not accepted.
- God warned Cain that unmastered sin waits like a predatory beast at the door.
- A pattern of resisting authority begins in early life and leads to ruin if unchecked.
- Rejecting God's correction brings painful discipline until one learns submissive humility.

### Sin Is Ready to Pounce
Author: Greg Laurie
Site: Crosswalk.com
URL: https://www.crosswalk.com/devotionals/harvestdaily/greg-laurie-devotion-september-9-2026.html
Passage: Genesis 4:7
Points:
- Sin is a constant predator ready to strike whenever believers let down their guard.
- Cain allowed wounded pride and anger over an offering to make him vulnerable.
- God gave Cain a proactive warning that sin was crouching to control him.
- Believers cannot defeat sin by willpower alone and must rely on God's strength.

### The Blood of Abel
Author: Ligonier Ministries
Site: Ligonier.org
URL: https://learn.ligonier.org/devotionals/blood-abel
Passage: Genesis 4:10
Points:
- Cain compounded his violent act by lying to God and disowning responsibility for his brother.
- Abel's shed blood cried out to God from the ground demanding justice.
- No human sin remains secret from God, who always hears the cries of the oppressed.
- Abel's blood called for retribution, but Christ's shed blood speaks a better word of redemption.

### The Only Remedy for Guilt
Author: Michael Youssef
Site: Crosswalk.com
URL: https://www.crosswalk.com/devotionals/leading-the-way/leading-the-way-week-of-june-17-2024.html
Passage: Genesis 4:9
Points:
- Cain wanted to approach God on his own terms rather than offering heartfelt obedience.
- Refusing God's warning, Cain let resentment drive him to murder and dishonest defiance.
- Running away from God only brought Cain perpetual restlessness and guilt.
- True relief from guilt comes solely through honest confession and repentance.
